mcqs.question: A circle with centre O and radius 7 cm is touched by a straight line at point P. Which point is the point of contact of the tangent line?

options.B: P (the point where the line meets the circle)
options.D: The foot of the perpendicular drawn from O to the line

mcqs.answer: P (the point where the line meets the circle)
mcqs.explanation: The point of contact of a tangent is the unique point where the tangent touches the circle. In the given situation that point is P. Option D describes the same point, but the definition of point of contact is precisely the point of touching, which is P. Options A and C are incorrect because the centre O is not on the tangent and not every point on the line is a point of contact.

mcqs.question: Why is the radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent always perpendicular to the tangent line?

options.A: Because the tangent is the shortest distance from the centre to the line
options.B: Because the radius is the longest line segment from the centre to the circle
options.C: Because if the radius were not perpendicular, the line would intersect the circle at another point, contradicting the definition of a tangent
options.D: Because the centre, the point of contact, and any other point on the tangent are collinear

mcqs.answer: Because if the radius were not perpendicular, the line would intersect the circle at another point, contradicting the definition of a tangent
mcqs.explanation: If the radius OP were not at right angles to the line, the line would cut the circle at two points, making it a secant, not a tangent. Hence the only way a line can touch the circle at exactly one point is when the radius to that point is perpendicular. Options A, B, and D do not correctly explain the geometric reason.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about a circle:

(i) From an external point A, the two tangents drawn to the circle have equal lengths.
(ii) The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact equals the angle in the alternate segment.

Which of the statements are true?
mcqs.explanation: Statement (i) follows from the tangent‑radius theorem: two tangents from the same external point are equal in length. Statement (ii) is the tangent‑chord theorem, which also follows from the same geometric principles. Hence both statements are correct. Options B, C, and D each miss one of the true statements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following descriptions correctly distinguishes a tangent from a secant of a circle?

options.A: A tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, whereas a secant meets the circle at exactly two distinct points.
options.B: A tangent meets the circle at exactly two points, whereas a secant meets the circle at exactly one point.
options.C: Both a tangent and a secant meet the circle at exactly one point, but a tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at that point.
options.D: A secant is a line that does not intersect the circle at all, while a tangent touches the circle at one point.

mcqs.answer: A tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, whereas a secant meets the circle at exactly two distinct points.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a tangent touches a circle at a single point, and a secant cuts the circle at two points. Option A states this correctly. Option B reverses the definitions. Option C incorrectly claims a secant also meets at one point. Option D incorrectly says a secant does not intersect the circle.
